excerpt: Check foreign ownership eligibility in Sharjah by confirming the buyer, exact project, type of right and registration with the relevant authority.
introduction:
Foreign ownership eligibility in Sharjah must be checked for the specific buyer and property. The emirate has approved real estate development areas and projects for ownership by non-citizens, but an advertisement or a general area name does not establish the right available for every unit. Ask Sharjah's Real Estate Registration Department to confirm the current status before paying.

This guide explains the evidence to request and the limits of published project counts. Rules, approved projects and transaction requirements can change; verify the current position for your circumstances.
takeaways: Confirm the exact project, unit, buyer's nationality and type of registered right with the Sharjah authority.
The 2022 decision reported by WAM concerns ownership in real estate development areas and projects, not an automatic right over every property.
Review the title or initial registration, seller authority, clearance and current transaction charges.

sections.heading: What did the 2022 decision say?
sections.body:
[Emirates News Agency reported](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hszrfs32-sharjah-executive-council-issues-decision-allowing) that Sharjah's Executive Council issued a decision in November 2022 allowing all nationalities to own real estate without a time limit in real estate development areas and projects, following a change to the registration law. The scope and current application must be confirmed for the property and buyer.

A separate [WAM report on the amended registration law](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hszrfrop-sharjah-ruler-amends-law-no-5-real-estate) describes ownership in development areas and projects under the council's regulations. It also describes other categories of ownership. Do not assume that all categories and rights have identical conditions.

Ask whether the interest is freehold, usufruct or another right, who can acquire it and how it will be registered. Use the sales brochure to identify the property and check its ownership terms with the authority.

sections.heading: Why must the project list be checked again?
sections.body:
WAM reports citing the Sharjah department described 47 approved projects by the end of Q1 2026, 50 by the end of H1 and 52 by the end of September. These are cumulative counts at different dates, not numbers to add together. They demonstrate that the reported list changed during the year.

The chart plots those reported checkpoints. A project count does not identify whether your unit is eligible, and it can become outdated. Request current confirmation from the department, including any conditions for the exact buyer and property.

The [Q1 report](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/bzpnrud-sharjah-real-estate-increases-407-reaching-aed185), [H1 report](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c18fnby-sharjah-real-estate-transactions-reach-aed295) and [nine-month report](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c2qm3mo-sharjah-real-estate-attracts-9891-new-investors) describe the respective counts.

sections.heading: How do you verify the unit?
sections.body:
Record the project name, registration details, building, unit number and seller or developer. Ask the department which documents it needs to confirm the buyer's right. Compare the official title or initial registration with the sale agreement and the identity and authority of the seller.

For a ready unit, check any mortgage, existing lease, building charges and required developer or management clearance. For an off-plan unit, review the registered project, contract, payment recipient, instalments and handover terms. Seek advice if the right being offered or a transfer condition is unclear.

The [Sharjah family area guide](/journal/best-areas-to-buy-property-in-sharjah-for-families) provides location context, but an area guide does not establish ownership eligibility for a particular apartment.

sections.heading: Check registration and costs
sections.body:
Ask the registration department and developer for an itemised current quote, the required documents, the parties responsible for each charge and the expected registration outcome. The Sharjah Executive Council's [property sale service listing](https://ec.shj.ae/en/government-service-details?serviceId=7804877f29e1d98d856134f4180a0517ef859c39c3ca891bc3a13e3773b7316bf5fcd08d2966872ceec3e0acf29842ff) describes a title transfer service; confirm its current applicability to the unit.

Do not apply a promotional exhibition rate or a fee quoted for another nationality to your transaction without confirmation. Add brokerage, finance, inspection and initial work where relevant, and keep a separate contingency.

If using a representative, check the required authority, notarisation and any translation. Verify payment instructions independently and retain receipts and the issued registration document.

sections.heading: What if the information is unclear?
sections.body:
Ask the authority for clarification before paying a reservation amount. Record the project and unit identifiers used in the enquiry and keep the response with the contract. If the seller's documents and official information disagree, resolve the discrepancy before proceeding.

A property purchase, a mortgage approval and a residence visa are separate decisions. Do not assume one automatically establishes the others. For legal or cross-border tax questions, consult an appropriately qualified adviser with the actual documents.

Review the confirmation if the buyer, property or transaction structure changes. A right verified for one unit or nationality should not be transferred to a different case without a new check.

sections.heading: Questions for the developer and registration department
sections.body:
Ask the developer for the project's official registration details and a copy of the unit's relevant ownership or initial-registration document. Confirm whether the seller is the registered holder and whether any instalment, mortgage or clearance remains outstanding. Take the exact identifiers to the department when checking eligibility.

Ask the department how the buyer's identity should be recorded, whether an authorised representative may sign and what documentation is required for the particular ownership right. If buying through a company, seek advice on the company's eligibility and registration rather than assuming the rules for an individual apply unchanged. Keep the answer and the date it was obtained.

sections.heading: Distinguish eligibility from availability
sections.body:
An approved development can contain many different units and phases. Approval of a project does not mean that the apartment shown in an advertisement is available, that its price is current or that the seller can transfer it immediately. Confirm the exact unit and the current contract position independently.

For an off-plan home, review the instalment schedule and delivery terms as well as ownership. For a ready home, inspect the condition and building costs. Eligibility is a necessary check, but it is only one part of the purchase decision.

sections.heading: Request current Sharjah options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your nationality, budget and intended use. Ask which units are currently available and request the project and registration details.

Confirm the current ownership right and official charges with the relevant Sharjah authority before committing.
